translations.text: In the month of Kanun, in the twentieth year, I was staying in Susa the citadel.
Hanani, one of my brothers, came with some Jewish men, and I asked them about the Jews who remained from the captivity and also about the city of Jerusalem.

The men I had questioned told me, “Those people who escaped from captivity are there in the city, living in great distress and deep disgrace. Jerusalem’s wall is broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire.”
When I heard these words, I sat down and wept. I mourned for many days, fasting and praying before the God of heaven.
I said, “I beg you, Lord, God of heaven, mighty, great, and awesome God, who preserves faithfulness and kindness toward those who love him and keep his commandments:

“Let your eyes now be open and your ears attentive to hear the prayer that I, your servant, pray before you day and night for the people of Israel, your servants. I confess the sins that the people of Israel have committed against you. Both I and my father’s household have sinned before you.
We have not kept the commandments and laws that you commanded your servant Moses.
“Remember the words you commanded your servant Moses, saying to him, ‘If you are unfaithful to me, I will scatter you among the nations.

“‘But if you return to me and keep my laws and carry them out, even if your scattered people are at the ends of heaven, I will gather you from there and bring you to the place I have chosen for my name to dwell.’
They are your servants and your people, whom you redeemed by your great power and your strong hand.

“Please, Lord, let your ear be attentive to your servant’s prayer and to the prayer of those who desire to fear your name. Deliver your servant today, and grant him mercy before this man.” Now I was the king’s cupbearer.
Then, in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, I was serving wine before the king. I took the wine and gave it to the king. I had not been sad in his presence.
The king said to me, “Why does your face look sad when you are not sick? This can only be sadness of heart.” I was very frightened.
I said to the king, “May the king live forever! Why should my face not look sad when the city containing my ancestors’ royal house lies in ruins and its gates have been burned with fire?”
And the king spoke to me about this. I pleaded and prayed before the God of heaven.
I said to the king, “If it pleases the king, I am your servant before you. Send me to Judah, to David’s city, to the burial place of my ancestors, so that I may rebuild it.”
The king said to me, “Fool, how long will you be away before you return?” It pleased the king to send me, and he gave me a set time.
I said to the king, “If it pleases the king, let letters be written for me to the governors beyond the River, so that they will assist me until I reach Judah,

“and a letter to Asaph, keeper of the king’s park, so that he will give me timber to make the gates of the house, and [?], and the city wall, and for the house I will occupy.” The king granted this to me because the hand of my God was good to me.
I came to the governor beyond the River and gave him the king’s letter. The king had sent army commanders and horsemen with me.
When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite heard, they were deeply upset that someone had come to seek the welfare of the people of Israel.
I came to Jerusalem and stayed there for three days.
I got up at night with the men who were with me. I had not told anyone what God had put in my heart to do for Jerusalem. There was no animal with me except the animal I was riding.
I went out at night through the Valley Gate, toward the Dragon Spring and the Dung Gate. I inspected Jerusalem’s walls, which were broken down, and its gates, which had been burned with fire.
I passed by the Valley Gate and the king’s canal, but there was no room for the animal to pass through there.
I went up through the valley at night, inspecting the wall. Then I came back, entered through the Valley Gate, and returned.
The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing. Until then I had told nothing to the Jews, the priests, the officials, the scribes, or the rest of those doing the work.
I said to them, “You see the distress we are in: Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned with fire. Come, let us rebuild Jerusalem’s wall so that we will no longer be a disgrace.”

I told them how the hand of my God had been with me for good, and also the words the king had spoken to me. They said, “We will rise and build!” And they strengthened their hands to do this good work.
When Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arab heard, they laughed at us and mocked us, saying, “What is this you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?”
I answered them, “The God of heaven will deliver us, and we will work, rise, and build. But you have no right, memorial, or share in Jerusalem.”

Eliashib the high priest arose, along with his fellow priests and his sons, at the Garden Gate. They installed its doors and consecrated them. They consecrated it as far as the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Tower of Hananel.
And as far as the boundary of the men of Jericho, and as far as the boundary of the sons of Zebur, Imri [?].
The sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate. They fitted it out and installed its doors, bolts, and bars.
Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired up to the boundary. Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel, repaired up to the boundary. Zadok son of Baana repaired up to the boundary.
The men of Tekoa repaired up to the boundary, but their leaders did not put their necks to the work of their masters.
Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besariah repaired the Second Gate. They fitted it out and installed its doors, bolts, and bars.
Melatiah the Gibeonite and Nadon the Merathite repaired up to the boundary. The men of Gibeon and Mizpah made a seat for the governor of the region beyond the River.
Uzziel son of Hadaiah, son of a goldsmith, repaired the boundary. Hananiah son of a perfumer repaired the boundary. They left Jerusalem with its wall widened.
Jeremiah son of Hur, ruler of Jerusalem, repaired the boundary.
Jedaiah son of Harumaph and the head of his household strengthened the adjoining section, and Hattush son of Hashabneiah strengthened the adjoining section.
Malchijah son of Harim and Hashum son of the ruler of Moab repaired a second stretch and the tower that remained.
Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of Jerusalem, repaired as far as the boundary, he and his sons.
Hanun, an inhabitant of Zioah, repaired the Valley Gate. They built it and installed its doors, bolts, and bars. There were a thousand cubits of wall as far as the Refuse Gate.
Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of Beth-haccherem, repaired the Refuse Gate. They built it and installed its doors, bolts, and bars.

Shallum son of Hozeh, ruler of Mizpah, repaired the Spring Gate. They built it, roofed it, and installed its doors, bolts, and bars. They also repaired the wall of the pool that supplies water to the king’s garden, as far as the stairway that descends from the City of David.
After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of Beth-zur, repaired as far as the path to David’s tomb, as far as the artificial pool, and as far as the House of the Warriors.
After him, the Levite Rehum son of Bani reinforced the wall as far as the boundary of Hashabiah, ruler of the entrance.
After him, their brothers reinforced the wall: Buzzi son of Hadar, ruler of Keilah.
He reinforced it as far as the boundary of Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah: a second section opposite the ascent that leads to the corner.
After him Baruch son of Zaccai took up the work and reinforced a second section, as far as the corner and as far as the entrance to the house of Eliashib the high priest.
After him Meremoth son of Uriah, of the family of Hakkoz, reinforced a second section, from the entrance to Eliashib’s house to the end of Eliashib’s house.
After him, the priests, the men of the valley, reinforced the wall.
After him Benjamin and Hasshub, the head of his household, reinforced it. After him Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, reinforced the section behind his house.
After him Bazzui son of Haidar reinforced a second section, from Azariah’s house to the corner and as far as the turning.
Of Palal son of Uzai [?], opposite the corner and as far as the Valley Tower that projects from the upper royal palace, and as far as the courtyard of the prison. After him, Pedaiah son of Parosh.
And the temple servants who lived in Ophel, as far as the Water Gate on the east and the projecting tower.
After him the men of Tekoa reinforced a second section, from opposite the great tower at the exit to the fortified wall.
From the entrance of the Horse Gate, the priests made repairs, each opposite his own house.
After them Zadok son of Immer reinforced the section opposite his house. After him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, keeper of the East Gate, reinforced it.

After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, reinforced a second section. After him Meshullam son of Berechiah reinforced the section opposite his house. After him Binnun son of Haidar reinforced a second section.
After him Malchijah son of a goldsmith reinforced the section as far as the house of the temple servants and the [?], opposite the Exit Gate, and as far as the ascent at the turning.
Between the ascent at the corner and the [?] Gate, the goldsmiths and merchants made repairs.
When Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he was distressed and became very angry, and he mocked the Jews.

He said to his fellow men and to the Samaritan army, “What are the Jews doing and boasting about? Let them offer sacrifices and eat on the day when they raise these stones from the heap of dirt, even though they are burned!”
Tobiah the Ammonite was standing beside him and said, “Whatever they build, I know that a fox will climb up and dislodge the stones of their walls.”
Hear, our God, for we have become a laughingstock. Turn their insults back on their own heads, and give them over to plunder in the land of their captivity.
Do not forgive their offenses, and do not let their sins be blotted out from before you, because they have raged against the building we are building.
We would rebuild the wall, and they built it, and the wall was completed to half its height. Then the mouths of all the people were opened to undertake the work.

Then, when Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that time had been given for the wall of Jerusalem to be rebuilt and that the gaps were beginning to be closed, they were very upset.
They all plotted together to come and fight against Jerusalem and cause trouble for its people.
We prayed before God that he would set guards over us by day and by night to protect us from them.
The Jews said, “The basket carriers' strength has failed, and there is far too much rubble. We cannot build the wall.”
Our enemies said, “They will neither know nor see until we fall upon them, kill them, and stop their work.”
The Jews who lived near them came and told us, “Look, by now they have come ten times to fight against you, from all the places where they were scattered.”
They came and stood behind the wall to fight against you with their arrows. They divided the force into clans, with their swords, spears, and bows.

I was afraid, but I stood up and said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Do not be afraid of them. Remember the great and fearsome Lord, and fight for your brothers and for your sons and daughters.”
Then, when our enemies heard that the matter had become known to us and that the Lord had frustrated their plans, we all returned and went up to the wall. We were all working, each at his own task.
From that day on, half the young men—half the people—did the work, while half held spears, shields, bows, and armor. The attendants stood behind the Jews.
Those building the wall and those carrying loads in baskets worked with one hand and carried a weapon in the other.
Each builder held a sword and stood building, and the man who sounded the horn stood behind him.
I said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, “The work is extensive and spread over a wide area. We are scattered along the wall, standing far apart from one another.”
Wherever you hear the sound of the horn, gather there with us, and our God will fight for us.”
We will carry on with our work, and half of us will hold spears from daybreak until the stars come out.
At that same time I also told the people that each man and his servant should spend the night in the streets of Jerusalem. They were to guard it by night and by day, and carry on with the work.
Neither I nor my brothers nor my servants nor the guards who followed me took off our clothes for a full month, each as it fell to him [?].
Then the people and their wives raised a loud outcry against their fellow Jews.
Some were saying, “Our sons, our daughters, and our brothers are many. Let us get grain so that we can eat and live.”
Some said, “We are selling our fields, houses, and vineyards to obtain grain during the famine and stay alive.”
Others were saying, “Let us borrow money from the king’s tax, cultivate our fields and vineyards, and live.”

Others said, “Our flesh is just like our brothers' flesh, and our children are just like their children. Yet now we are subjecting our sons and daughters to slavery. Some of our daughters have been subjected to service as slave women, and they do not lift their hands before God. Our fields, vineyards, and possessions are being given to others.”
I was deeply distressed when I heard their outcry and these words.
My heart was broken within me, but I controlled my temper and spoke with the elders and the nobles.

I said to them, “We are buying back our fellow Jews who are being sold to the nations, both them and their children, yet you are taking your own brothers.” Because of this I raised my voice against them and said to them, “Will you too sell your brothers?” They were silent and gave me no answer.
I said to them, “What you are doing is not good. You are not walking in the fear of our God, for you are acting like the nations around us.”
Let me, my sons, and my brothers also take money, buy grain, and leave it for the poor among our people.
Let us return their fields, vineyards, olive trees, and houses to them, and let us relinquish the money, grain, wine, and oil to the rest of the people.
They said to me, “We will do as you say.” I called the priests and told them that this was what ought to be done, and I made them swear to act according to this declaration.

And also to the young men [?]. They said, “May God shake out of his house and his labor every man who does not keep this promise. May he be shaken out and left empty in this way.” All the people said, “Amen.” All the people stood up and praised the Lord, and all the people acted according to this declaration.

Moreover, from the day he appointed me governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes, twelve years, I and my brothers—I was their leader—took no donkey belonging to any of them, nor did I harm any of them.

The governors before me subjected the people to forced service and took wine, bread, and a large amount of silver from them as tribute, as much as forty shekels. They also gave their servants authority over the people, and these exercised power over them and mistreated them. But I did not act this way, because I feared God.
I also devoted myself vigorously to the work on this wall, and I bought no fields. All the young men, the sons of the Jews, gathered and stood there at the work.
And the nobles and officials, 150 men, and those who came to us from the peoples around us came to us, each at his table.

The man who prepared the food would bring it to the laborers who were working. One ox, six fat sheep, and birds were prepared for us, and once every ten days there was wine in abundance. Despite this, I did not ask for food or authority, because the work weighed heavily on this people.
Remember me for good, my God, for everything I have done for this people.

Then, when Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that we had rebuilt the wall and that there was no breach in it—although up to that time we had not yet erected the doorposts of the gates—
Sanballat and Geshem sent word to me, saying, “Come, let us go together and camp like a troop in the plain of Ono.” But they were planning to harm me.
I sent a messenger to them and said, “I am doing a great work and cannot come down, lest it stop when I leave it and come down to you.”
They sent me this same message four times, and I gave them the same answer.
Sanballat sent his servant to me a fifth time with the same message and a letter in his hand.

It was written in it: “It has been reported among the nations, and Geshem says, that you and the Jews are planning to rebel. That is why you are building the wall, and according to these reports you are to become their king.
You have also appointed prophets to prophesy about you in Jerusalem, saying, ‘Look, Ezra has become king in Judah!’ Now reports like these have reached the king. So come, let us consult together.”
I sent word to him and said, “What you are saying is not true; you are saying these things out of your own imagination.”
For they were all trying to frighten us, saying, “Their hands will grow weak and leave the work.” They were telling us not to do it. Now strengthen my hands!

I went into the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel, who was confined there. He said to me, “Come, let us meet in the house of the LORD, inside the temple, and shut the temple doors, because they are coming to kill you. They are coming at night to kill you.”
I said, “Should a man like me run away? Far be it from me to run away and enter the temple!”

But I knew that God had not sent him against me, nor had I been told through a prophet that someone would kill me. Tobiah, Sanballat, and his companions had hired him and sent him against me to kill me.
He had been hired so that I would be afraid and act that way and sin, giving them grounds for a bad report with which to disgrace me.
Remember, my God, Tobiah, Sanballat, and his companions according to these hateful deeds of theirs. Remember also Jedaiah the prophet and the rest of the prophets who were making me afraid of them.
The wall was finished on the twenty-fifth of Elul, in fifty-two days.
Then, when all our enemies heard, all the nations around us were afraid and trembled greatly before us. They knew that this work had been accomplished by God.
In those days the nobles of the Jews were also sending many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah’s letters were coming to them.

For there were many people in Judah who had sworn to him that they would not oppose him, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
They also spoke of his good words in my presence, and they reported to him what I said. Tobiah himself kept sending letters to frighten me.
Then, when the wall had been built, the gates erected, and the doorposts set up, and the gatekeepers, attendants, and Levites had been put in place,
I gave orders to my brother Hanani and to Hananiah, the commander of the fortress of Jerusalem, because he was an upright man who feared God and turned away from evil.

I said to them, “The gates of Jerusalem must not be opened until the sun is up. While it is still daylight, the gates must be shut and secured. The inhabitants of Jerusalem are to stand guard, each at his post and each opposite his own house.”
The city was large and spacious, but there were few people in it, and they had no houses built.

My God put it into my heart, and I assembled the nobles and the leaders of the people according to their family lines. I found the genealogical record of those who had come up at first, and I found this written in it:
These are the people of the province who came up from captivity in exile, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had deported. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town.
They came up with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nehemiahel, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nahtum, and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
The descendants of Parosh: two thousand one hundred seventy-two.
The descendants of Shephatiah: 372.
The descendants of Arah: 652.
The descendants of Pahath-moab, belonging to the descendants of Jeshua and Joab: 2,818.
The descendants of Elam: 1,254.
The descendants of Zattu: 854.
The descendants of Zaccai: 760.
The descendants of Bani: 644.
The descendants of Bebai: 628.
The descendants of Azgad: 2,322.
The descendants of Adonikam: 667.
The descendants of Bigvai: 2,067.
The descendants of Adin: 655.
The descendants of Ater, of Hezekiah's family: 98.
The descendants of Hashum: 328.
The descendants of Bezai: 324.
The descendants of Huram: 112.
The descendants of Gibeon: 95.
The men of Bethlehem and Netophah: 188.
The men of Anathoth: 128.
The men of Beth-armuth: 42.
The men of Beth-nearin, Chephirah, and Beeroth: 743.
The men of Geba and Ramah: 721.
The men of Michmash: 122.
The men of Bethel and Ai: 123.
The men of Nebo: 52.
Those of the house of Elam: 1,254.
The descendants of Harim: 320.
The descendants of Jericho: three hundred and forty-five.
The descendants of Lod and Ono: 721.
The descendants of Senaah: 3,930.
The priests: the descendants of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua: 973.
The descendants of Immer: 1,052.
The descendants of Pashhur: 1,247.
The descendants of Hadum: 1,017.
The Levites, the descendants of Jeshua belonging to Kadmiel, of the descendants of Hodiah: 74.
The ministers, the descendants of Asaph: 148.
The gatekeepers: the descendants of Shallum, the descendants of Ater, the descendants of Talmon, the descendants of Akkub, the descendants of Hatita, and the descendants of Shobai: 138.
The men: the descendants of Ziha, the descendants of Hasupha, and the descendants of Tabbaoth.
The descendants of Keros, the descendants of Sia, and the descendants of Peron.
The descendants of Lebana, the descendants of Hagaba, and the descendants of Shalmai.
The descendants of Hanani, the descendants of Adda, and the descendants of Hagar.
The descendants of Ana, the descendants of Rezin, and the descendants of Dekora.
The descendants of Gazzam, the descendants of Adda, and the descendants of Paseah.
The descendants of Besai, the descendants of Meunim, and the descendants of Japhusin.
The descendants of Bakbuk, the descendants of Hakupha, and the descendants of Harhur.
The descendants of Bazluth, the descendants of Mehida, and the descendants of Harsha.
The descendants of Bazuk, the descendants of Sisera, and the descendants of Temah.
The descendants of Neziah and the descendants of Hatipha.
The descendants of Solomon’s servants: the descendants of Sotai, the descendants of Sophereth, and the descendants of Peruiah.
The descendants of Jaala, the descendants of Darkon, and the descendants of Giddel.
The descendants of Shephatiah, the descendants of Hattil, the descendants of Cabroth, the descendants of Zebaim, and the descendants of Amon.
All the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon’s servants: 392.
These are the people who came up from Tel-melah to Tel-aba and to Cherub. They made their statement but could not establish their ancestral families or their descent, only that they were from Israel.
The descendants of Bani, the descendants of Delaiah, the descendants of Tobiah, and the descendants of Dekora: 642.

And from the priests: the descendants of Hananiah, the descendants of Hakkoz, and the descendants of Barzillai, who had married one of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
These men searched for their names in the record of their family lines but did not find them, and they were excluded from the priesthood.
The elders of the priests told them not to eat any of the most holy things until a high priest arose who could inquire and discern.
The whole assembly together numbered 42,470.
Besides their male and female slaves, who numbered 7,333 in all, there were 245 male and female attendants.
There were 435 camels and 6,720 donkeys.
Some of the heads of ancestral families contributed to the work on the house. The elders of the priests gave to the treasury 1,000 gold darics, fifty bowls, and 530 priestly tunics.
Some of the heads of ancestral families gave to the treasury for the work 20,000 gold darics and 2,200 minas of silver.
The rest of the people gave 20,000 gold darics, 2,000 minas of silver, and sixty-seven priestly tunics.

The priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the attendants, some of the people, the temple servants, and all Israel returned to their towns. When the seventh month arrived, the Israelites were in their towns.
All the people gathered as one in the square in front of the Water Gate. They told Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the Law of Moses, which the LORD had commanded Israel to follow.
Ezra the priest brought the book of the Law before the people, both men and women and everyone prepared to listen, on the first day of the seventh month.

He read the book in the square at the Water Gate from morning until midday, before the men and women and those who could listen. The people's ears were attentive, and they listened to the commandments of the Law.

Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform that he had made to speak from. Beside him stood Mattithiah, Shema, Ananiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah on his right. On his left stood Peraiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashabiah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
Ezra the scribe opened the book of the Law in the sight of all the people, for he was above all the people. When he opened it, all the people stood up.
Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God, and all the people answered, saying, “Amen and amen!” They raised their hands, then knelt and worshiped before the LORD with their faces to the ground.

Jeshua and his sons, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabar, Hanani, Paniah, and the Levites ministered to the people in the Law, while the people stood in their places.
They read from the book of the Law of the LORD as it lay open, and the people were instructed in it and understood what was read.

Nehemiah, the chief of the priests, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were ministering to the people said to all the people, “Today is holy before the LORD your God. Do not grieve or weep.” For all the people were weeping as they heard the book of the Law.

He said to them, “Go, eat and drink, and send food to anyone who has nothing prepared, because today is holy before the LORD. Do not grieve, because it is a day of joy in the LORD, and he will be your helper.”
The Levites quieted all the people, saying, “Be quiet, because today is holy, and do not weep.”
All the people went away to eat and drink, to send food, and to celebrate with great joy. They accepted the words that had been made known to them.

On the second day, the heads of the ancestral families of all the people, together with the priests and Levites, gathered around Ezra the scribe to gain understanding from him about the book of the Law.
They found in the book of the Law that the LORD had commanded Moses that the Israelites should live in shelters during the festival in the month of Tishri.

To make this known, they had heralds proclaim in all their towns and in Jerusalem: “Go up to the mountain and bring olive branches, walnut branches, palm leaves, citron leaves, and willow branches. Make shelters, as it is written in the book of the Law of Moses.”

The people went out and brought them and made shelters for themselves, each on his roof, in their courtyards, in the courtyard of the house of the LORD, in the square at the Water Gate, and in the square at the Ephraim Gate.
All the people who had returned from captivity made shelters and lived in them, for the Israelites had not done this from the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day. There was very great joy.

They read from the book of the Law of the LORD every day, from the first day to the last. They celebrated the festival for seven days, and on the eighth day they gathered together, as had been written for them.
On the twenty-fourth day of this same month, the Israelites gathered with fasting and sackcloth, and they put ashes on themselves.
The descendants of Israel separated themselves from all the other peoples. They stood and confessed their sins and the sins of their ancestors.

They stood in their places and read from the book of the law of the LORD their God. For a quarter of the day they read, and for a quarter of the day they confessed and worshiped before the LORD their God.
The leaders over the Levites—Jeshua and Kadmiel, the sons of Hashabiah, and Sherebiah, the sons of Chenani—stood up and prayed aloud before the LORD their God.

The Levites—Jeshua and Kadmiel, the sons of Hashabiah, and Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shecaniah, and Pethahiah—said, “Stand up and bless the LORD their God from everlasting to everlasting. Blessed is his glorious name, exalted above all created beings and all praise.

You alone are the LORD. You made the heavens, the highest heavens and all their hosts, the earth and everything on it, and the waters and everything in them. You give life to them all, and the hosts of heaven worship you.
You are the LORD God who chose Abram, brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans, and changed his name to Abraham.

You found his heart pure before you and swore oaths to him to give him the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, Jebusites, and Girgashites—to give it to his descendants. You fulfilled your words to him, because you are righteous.
You saw the enslavement of our ancestors in Egypt and heard their outcry at the Red Sea.

You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, his entire army, and all the people of his land, because you knew that they had acted arrogantly against your people. You made a name for yourself that remains to this day.
You split the sea before them, and they crossed through the sea on dry ground. You drowned their pursuers in the depths of the sea, as a stone sinks in mighty waters.
You led them by a pillar of cloud during the day and by a pillar of fire at night, to light the path for them to walk on.
You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven. You gave them just judgments, true laws, and good statutes and commandments.
You made known to them your holy Sabbath and the commandments, statutes, and laws that you commanded them through Moses your servant.
You gave them bread from heaven for their hunger and water from a rock for their thirst. You told them to enter and take possession of the land that your hand had prepared to give them.
But they and their ancestors acted arrogantly, became stubborn, and did not obey your commandments.

They refused to listen and did not remember the wonders you had done for them. Their hearts turned to their evil deeds. But you are a forgiving, compassionate, and gracious God, slow to anger and ready to hear prayer, and you did not abandon them.
For they made a cast-metal calf and said, ‘This is your God, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt,’ and they committed great evils.

Yet in your great compassion you did not abandon them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not leave them during the day, guiding them on their way, nor did the pillar of fire at night, lighting the path they were to follow.
You gave your good Spirit to teach them. You did not withhold manna from their mouths, and you gave them water for their thirst.
For forty years you let them lack nothing in the wilderness. Their clothes did not wear out, and their sandals did not split.
You gave them the kingdoms of the nations and apportioned them to each person. They took possession of the land of Sihon, the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og, king of Bashan.
You made their children as numerous as the stars in heaven and brought them into the land that you had told their ancestors to enter and possess.

Their children entered and took possession of the land. You crushed before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and handed them over to them, along with their kings and the peoples of the land, to do with them as they pleased.

They captured fortified towns and fertile land. They took possession of houses full of every good thing, cisterns already dug, vineyards, olive trees, and abundant fruit trees. They ate, were satisfied, grew fat, and delighted in your great goodness.
But they turned away and acted falsely toward you. They cast your law out of their minds and killed your prophets because they told them to return to you. They committed great evils.

You handed them over to their enemies, who oppressed them. In their time of distress they pleaded with you, and you heard them from heaven in your great compassion. You raised up deliverers for them, who rescued them from the hands of their oppressors.

But when you gave them relief, they again did what was hateful in your sight. You abandoned them to their enemies, who enslaved them. Again they prayed before you, and you heard from heaven and rescued them every time, according to your abundant compassion.

You warned them to bring them back to your laws, but they acted arrogantly and did not obey your commandments. They sinned against your judgments, by which a person will live if they carry them out. They stubbornly turned their shoulders away, stiffened their necks, and would not listen.
You preached to them for many years and warned them by your Spirit through your prophets, but they did not listen. So you handed them over to the peoples of the surrounding lands.
But because of your great mercy, you did not destroy them or abandon them, for you are a gracious and compassionate God.

Now, our God, the great, mighty, and awesome God, who keeps his oaths and remains faithful, do not let all the distress that has come upon us be hidden from your sight—upon our kings, our leaders, our priests, our prophets, our ancestors, and all the people, from the days of the king of Assyria until today.
You are just in everything that has come upon us, for you are indeed truthful, while we have acted arrogantly.
Our kings, our leaders, our priests, and our ancestors did not follow your law or listen to your commandments and the warnings you gave them.
They rejected your kingship and the great goodness you had shown them in the good, fertile land you gave them. They did not serve you or turn away from their evil deeds.
Because of this, we are slaves today. As for the land you gave our ancestors so that they could eat its fruit and enjoy its good things, here we are, working within it as slaves.
The kings you have placed over us because of our sins take its produce. They rule over our bodies and our livestock as they please, and we live in great distress.
Because of all these things, we swear in good faith and bear witness to the seal—we, our elders, the Levites, and our priests.
And all those of us who survived: Nehemiah the elder, son of Hananiah, the chief priest, and Zerahiah;
and Seraiah, Azariah, and Jeremiah;
and Pashhur, Jeremiah, Malchijah, and Peshtiah;
and Hattush, Shecaniah, and Malluch;
and Shecum, Azmaveth, and Gebariah;
Daniel, Gibbethon, Baruch;
Meshullam, Abijah, Benjamin;
Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah. These were the priests.
And the Levites: Jeshua son of Jezaniah, the sons of Mabbani, Hader the first;
and their brothers: Shecaniah, Uriah, Kelita, Pelatiah, Hanani;
Mica, Rechub, Hashabiah;
Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shecaniah;
Hodiah, the sons of Bani.
The leaders of the people: Parosh, the ruler of Moab, Elam, Zattu;
the sons of Azgar and the sons of Adonijah.
Bigvai, Adin.
Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur.
Uriah, Hashum, Bezai.
Hoziph, Anathoth, Nebai.
Magpiash, Meshullam, Aziphi.
Meshezabel, Zadok, Jehoiada.
Pelatiah, Hanani, Ananiah.
Hoshea, Hananiah, Jeshua.
Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek.
Rehum, Hashabiah, Maaseiah.
Ahijah, Hanani, Anan.
Malluch, Harim, Baanah.

The rest of the people—the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, ministers, servants, and everyone who has separated from the peoples of the surrounding lands—are to come to the law of the LORD: they, their wives, their sons, their daughters, and everyone who has knowledge and understanding.

They stand firmly with their brothers and relatives and enter into an oath and a covenant to walk according to the law of the LORD, which he gave through Moses, the servant of the LORD, and to observe and carry out all the commandments, judgments, and laws of the LORD our Lord.
We will not give our daughters to the peoples of the land or take their daughters as wives for our sons.

They shall not take what the peoples of the land bring. Anyone who hires out an animal on the Sabbath day shall not collect a fee. We shall not carry a load on the Sabbath day, because it is holy. We shall forgive everything owed to us; in the seventh year we shall forgive it.
We imposed on ourselves the obligation to give a third of a stater each week for the service of the house of our God.

For the bread set apart, for the regular offerings and the regular burnt offering, for the Sabbaths, new moons, festivals, sacred things, and the forgiveness of Israel's sins, and for all the work of the house of our God.
We—the priests, Levites, and people—cast lots concerning the offerings of wood, to bring them to the house of the LORD our God, as it is written in the book of the law.
To bring the firstfruits of our land and the first of all the fruit of the trees, year after year, and to bring them to the house of the LORD.

The firstborn of our sons and our livestock, as it is written in the law of the LORD, and the firstborn of our cattle and flocks, to bring them to the house of our God, to the priests who minister in the house of our God.

We shall give the first of our dough, the produce of our threshing floors, the fruit of all our trees, wine, and oil to the priests who minister before our God. We shall give a tenth of the produce of our lands to the Levites, and the Levites shall collect the tithes from all the villages where we work.
A priest descended from Aaron shall be with the Levites when they collect their tithes, and the Levites shall take a tenth to the house of our God, to the storerooms and the treasury.

For the Israelites and the descendants of Levi shall bring the firstfruits of grain, wine, and oil to the storerooms. The sacred vessels are there, and the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, and guards shall not abandon the house of our God.

The elders of the people shall live in Jerusalem, and the rest of the people shall cast lots to bring one person in ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city, while the other nine parts shall live in the villages.
The people blessed all those who willingly chose to live in Jerusalem.

These are the leaders of the city who lived in Jerusalem and in the villages of Judah. They lived, each on his own inherited property, in their villages: the Israelites, priests, Levites, the people, and the descendants of Solomon's servants.

In Jerusalem, from the descendants of Judah and from the descendants of Benjamin, and from the descendants of Hodiah: Nethaniah son of Uzziah, son of Zechariah, son of Amariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Mahalalel, from the descendants of Perez.
Maaseiah son of Baruch, son of Col-hozeh, son of Adaiah, son of Azariah, son of Jonadab, son of Zechariah, son of Shelah.
All the descendants of Perez who lived in Jerusalem numbered 468 valiant men.
These are the descendants of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Joiada, son of Peraiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Naasiah, son of Anthiel, son of Isaiah.
And after him, 928.
Joel son of Zechariah was in charge of them, and Judah son of Senuah was in charge of the city’s second quarter.
From the priests: Berechiah son of Joiada,
Seraiah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, who was in charge of the house of the LORD.
His fellow priests who performed the work inside numbered 822. Also Azariah son of Jeroham, son of Pelaniah, son of Amzar, son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah.
Their fellow priests, heads of their ancestral households, numbered 242. Also Amashai son of Azarel, son of Ahdi, son of Meshillemoth, son of Immer.
Their brothers, mighty warriors, numbered 128. In charge of them was Zabdiel, son of the nobles.
From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Jeshua, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, son of Bani,
son of Shabbethai; and Jozabar, who was in charge of the outside work of the house of the Lord and was among the leaders of the Levites.
Mattaniah son of Mica son of Zabdi son of Asaph, the foremost leader of the Jews in prayer; Bakbukiah, second among his brothers; and Ira son of Shammua son of Galal son of Jethron.
All the Levites in the holy city numbered 284.
And second were Akkub and Talmon and their brothers who guarded the gate, numbering 172.
The rest of Israel, and the priests and Levites, were in all the towns of Judah, each on his own inherited property.
Their servants lived each at his work and on his farmland.

The supervisor of the Levites in Jerusalem was Abdi son of Bunni son of Hashabiah son of Mattaniah son of Mica, from the descendants of Asaph, who ministered in connection with the work of the house of the Lord.
For the king's command applied to them, and a fixed provision was established for those who served, day by day.
Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, from the descendants of Zerah son of Judah, was in charge of everyone the king designated concerning the entire accounting of the people.
As for their settlements and their fields, some of the descendants of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba and its villages, in Ribon and its villages, and in Kabzeel and its villages.
in Hoshea, Moladah, and Beth-pelet;
in Hazar-shua, Beersheba, and its villages;
in Zankela, Mekiah, and its villages;
in En-rimmon, Zedah, and Jarmuth;
Also in Zioah and Adullam and their villages, in Lachish and its villages, and in Azekah and its villages. They settled from Beersheba as far as the Valley of Hinnom.
The descendants of Benjamin were from Ramah of Michmash, Ai, and Bethel and its villages;
Anathoth, Joab, and Ananiah;
Hazor, Ramah, and Gittaim.
And Hadar, Zeboim, and Jeballat.
And Lod, Ono, Niha, and Harsha.
And among the Levites were divisions of Judah and Benjamin.
These are the priests and Levites who came up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua: Seraiah, Azma, Ezra,
Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
Iddo, Azzath, Abijah,
Benjamin, Maadariah, Bilgai,
Shemaiah, Naddub, Jedaiah,
Sallai, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah. These were the heads of the priests and their brothers in the days of Jeshua.
The Levites: Jeshua and his sons, Kadmiel, Arabiah, Judah, Mattaniah, Hodith [?]—he and his brothers.
And Bakbukiah, Eli, and their brothers stood opposite them on watch.
Jeshua fathered Joiakim, Joiakim fathered Eliashib, and Eliashib fathered Joiada.
Joiada fathered Jonathan, and Jonathan fathered Jaddua.
In the days of Joiakim, the priests who were heads of ancestral families were: Seraiah, Amariah, Jeremiah, Hananiah,
Ezra, Meshullam, Amariah, Johanan,
Malchijah, Jonathan, Shecaniah, Joseph,
Harim, Ariah, Meroth, Lahmi,
Iddo, Zechariah, Gaathon, Meshullam,
Abijah, Zichri, Benjamin, Modiah, Pilta,
Bilgah, Shammua, Shemaiah, Jonathan,
Joiada, Mattani, Jedaiah, Uzzi,
Sallai, Kallai, Amok, Ammi,
Hilkiah, Hashabiah, Hoda, Nethanel.
In the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Joiada, the heads of the ancestral families of the Levites were recorded, as were the priests during the reign of Darius the Persian.
The heads of the ancestral families of the descendants of Levi were recorded in the book of the daily events, down to the days of Johanan son of Eliashib.

The leaders of the Levites were Ishbil, Sherebiah, and Jeshua, with his brothers, the descendants of Kadmiel, opposite them, praising and giving thanks according to the commands of David, the prophet of the Lord, one watch opposite another.
Mattaniah, Bukki, Obadiah, Shallum, Talmon, and Akkub, the gatekeeper.
These served in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiel the governor and Ezra the priest and scribe.

When the wall of Jerusalem was finished, they gathered the Levites throughout their territory to bring them to Jerusalem and to celebrate with gladness, thanksgiving, songs of praise, cymbals, and lyres.
The sons of the ministers gathered from the plain around Jerusalem and from the settlement of Netophah,
And from Beth-gilgal, from the valley of Geba, and from Aramoth, because the ministers had built settlements for themselves around Jerusalem.
The priests and Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people and the gates of the wall.
They brought the leaders of Judah up onto the wall and appointed two large companies. They walked along the top of the wall to the right, from the Great Gate.
Hoshaiah went with them, along with half the leaders of Judah,
and Azriel, Ezra, and Meshullam,
and Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah,
From among the descendants of the priests, with trumpets, was Zechariah son of Jonathan son of Shemaiah son of Mattaniah son of Maacah son of Zaccur son of Asaph.

With his brothers Shemaiah, Azriel, Milalai, Gilalai, Ataz, Nethanel, Hanani, and Judah, carrying the musical instruments for the praises of David, the prophet and servant of the Lord. Ezra the scribe went ahead of them.
Above the Fountain Gate, directly ahead of them, they went up the ascent of the City of David, by the ascent of the wall above David’s house, to the great eastern gate.
They gave thanks and went up above, with me following them. Half the people went up onto the wall and stood at the Great Tower and on the high wall above the Broad Wall.
And above the Gate of Ephraim as far as the Old Gate and the Fishermen’s Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel as far as the High Tower and the Garden Gate. They stopped at the Great Gate.
The two assemblies entered the house of the Lord, along with me and half the officials who were with me,
and the priests Eliakim and Maaseiah, [?], Micah, Elihu, Anani, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with horns,
Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Johanan, Malchijah, Elam, Azzur, and Shammua were the ministers, and Zerahiah was their leader.
That day they offered great sacrifices and rejoiced, because the Lord had given them great joy. The women and children also rejoiced, and the rejoicing in Jerusalem could be heard far away.

That day they appointed men who made payments to the king from the treasuries to oversee the storehouses, to collect in them the firstfruits and tithes of the village leaders, as written in the book of the law for the priests and Levites. For the Jews rejoiced over the priests and Levites who were serving.
They carried out their duties in the house of their God and kept their watches in purity, along with the ministers and gatekeepers, according to the command of David and his son Solomon.
For Asaph lived in the days of David and stood at the head of the ministers, praising and giving thanks before the Lord God.

In the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah, all Israel gave gifts to the ministers and gatekeepers, bringing them out and giving them day by day. They set apart offerings for the Levites, and the Levites set apart offerings for the descendants of Aaron.
That very day the book of the law of Moses was read aloud to the people, and it was found written in it that Ammonites and Moabites must never enter the assembly of the Lord.
For they had not met the Israelites with bread and water, but had hired Balaam to curse them. Yet our God turned his curses into blessings.
Then, when they heard the words of the law, all those of mixed ancestry were separated from Israel.
Then Eliashib the priest came.

He built a large courtyard for him there. Previously, the offerings, frankincense, vessels for the tithes of grain, wine, and oil, the firstfruits for the Levites, attendants, and gatekeepers, and the priests’ first offerings had been stored there.
During all this I was not in Jerusalem, because in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes, king of Babylon, I had gone to the king. After some time I requested leave from the king.
I came to Jerusalem and learned of the evil Eliashib had done for Tobiah by making a house for him in the courtyard of the LORD.
I was greatly displeased, and I threw all the furnishings of Tobiah’s house into the street, outside the courtyard.
I gave orders, and they purified the courtyard. Then I brought back there the vessels of the Lord’s house, the offerings, and the frankincense.
I learned that the Levites’ portion was not being given to them, and the Levites, attendants, and workers had fled, each to his own field.
I confronted the leaders and said to them, “Why has the house of the LORD been abandoned?” I gathered them and stationed them at their posts.
All the Jews brought the tithes of grain, wine, and oil into the storehouses.

I put Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Peraiah, one of the Levites, in charge of the storehouses, and with them Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah. They were considered trustworthy, and it fell to their lot to be in charge of their fellow workers.
Remember me, my God, for this, and do not erase the good deeds I have done in the house of my God and in carrying out its duties.

In those days I saw caravans traveling in Judah on the Sabbath, bringing loads carried on donkeys. They were also bringing wine, grapes, figs, and loads into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. I warned them, “Do not sell provisions.”
“Do not bring fish, and do not buy or sell on the Sabbath to the people of Judah in Jerusalem.”
I confronted the leaders of Judah and said to them, “Why are you doing this evil thing and profaning the Sabbath day?
Your ancestors acted this way, and God brought all this disaster upon us and upon this city. Yet you are adding fury and wrath against Israel by profaning the Sabbath day.”

Then, when the gates of Jerusalem were opened before the Sabbath, I ordered the gates to be shut. I ordered that the gates should not be opened until after the Sabbath, and I stationed some of my servants at the gates so that no load would enter on the Sabbath day.
The merchants and sellers of merchandise spent the night outside Jerusalem for a day or two.

I warned them and said to them, “Why do you not enter at the gate in the wall while it is still daylight? If you disregard this instruction, I will lay hands on you.” From that time onward they did not enter on the Sabbath.

I told the Levites to purify themselves and come in as guards and gatekeepers to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember this also in my favor, my God, and have pity on me according to your abundant mercy.
Also in those days I saw Jews who had married foreign women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
Half their children spoke the language of Ashdod, and half knew how to speak the language of Judah, but according to the language of the nations.

I confronted them and cursed them. I killed some of their men and buried them. I made them swear by God: “You must not give your daughters to their sons or take any of their daughters for your sons. Woe to you!

It was because of these things that Solomon, king of Israel, sinned. Among the many nations there was no king like him. He was loved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel. Yet foreign women caused even him to sin.
You heard the word, yet you committed this great evil, acting unfaithfully toward our God and marrying foreign women.”
One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, was a son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite, and I drove him away from me.
Remember them, my God, for the defilement of the priesthood and for the defilement of the priests and Levites.
I purified them from all the nations and stationed the priests and Levites at their posts, each at his work,
and for the offerings and holy gifts at their appointed times and festivals, and for the firstborn. Remember this kindness in my favor, my God. The writing of the book of Ezra the scribe is finished.
